newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebel spokesman denies easing demands.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel spokesman denies easing demands.

text.p: The international spokesman for the rebels holding 72 hostages on Sunday denied Peru's claims the group had "implicitly" dropped their main demand that their jailed comrades be released, but he said they acknowleged they would not achieve all of their demands.

"There is nothing implicit. (President Alberto) Fujimori is misinterpreting what we have said from the beginning that our global proposal is negotiable," MRTA spokesman Isaac Velazco told Reuters in a telephone interview from Hamburg. "We are not going to maintain our global proposal 100 percent."

Fujimori said in interviews on Saturday he was optimistic of restarting talks with the the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels because they had "implicitly" agreed not to include the demand for the release of over 400 jailed comrades.
The rebels have also demanded improved prison conditions, an overhaul of Peru's secret court system for people accused of terrorism and an end to Fujimori's free-market economic reforms.

"In negotiation there have to be concessions. We are not trying to impose on the government but nor do we want the government to impose on us," Velazco said. "We have to arrive at points that satisfy both sides."

Fujimori refuses to consider the main demand, but has said he is willing to discuss improving prison conditions and allowing the rebels to go into exile in another country, if they free all 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
